She is known for her contributions to the Sanskrit language, particularly in the fields of poetry and music. Architha's works have been preserved in various anthologies and have influenced generations of poets and musicians. She is also revered for her wisdom and beauty, which were said to have captivated many powerful rulers and nobles of her time.

According to Hindu mythology, Architha is an incarnation of the goddess Saraswati, the deity of knowledge, music, and arts. In this form, Architha is believed to have imparted the wisdom of the Vedas and the arts of music and poetry to the great sage Valmiki, who went on to compose the epic Ramayana. This mythological reference places Architha in the ancient Indian tradition of divine patronage of human artistic and intellectual pursuits.
